wiki-iran.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It is a measure of public attention rather than events, and it rises when something puts the country in front of readers who do not normally follow it.
wiki-iran.recent: Readership has fallen by roughly two fifths since the 19 July peak, settling at its lowest level of the window on 13 August even as the Strait of Hormuz story continued: Iran legislated control of the strait through a statute rather than a blockade, the Guard Corps said it downed a US MQ-9 Reaper near Bandar Abbas, and Brent rose 12 cents on blockade news.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is sold against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Hormuz has dominated the price without breaking it: Iran's blockade announcement moved Brent 12 cents, and Tehran has since legislated control of the strait rather than closing it. Two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz on 13 August, and the war-risk premium has reached Pakistan's pumps, where diesel now costs 383.95 rupees a litre.

wti.standing: The US benchmark crude, priced at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the barrel American refiners and shale producers settle against. It sets the floor under petrol, diesel and jet fuel across North America, and moves on supply shocks and inventory swings.
wti.recent: Crude has fallen roughly a quarter from its May peak even as strikes multiplied: drones hit Libya's Zawiya refinery and Russia's Nizhnekamsk, two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz, and Iran's Azizi issued threats over the strait. Prices eased on Hormuz reopening hopes, with the war premium showing up in diesel — $5.36 a gallon in the US — rather than in the barrel.

natgas-hh.standing: The US benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline hub and the reference for most American gas contracts. It sets the cost of winter heating, of gas-fired electricity, and of the LNG the US ships abroad.
natgas-hh.recent: The series drifted down through the summer to a low of $2.56 on Aug 7, and the demand story in the coverage is forward-looking rather than immediate: SpaceX is building its own natural gas power plants for a Texas chip factory, and Amazon is funding a Fort Stockton plant whose 35 turbines could emit 33 million tons yearly.

wheat.standing: A benchmark price for a tonne of milling wheat, the grain that feeds more people directly than any other. It sets the cost of bread, flour and animal feed, and it moves on harvests, export policy and whether grain can leave the ports it is stored in.
wheat.recent: Two supply shocks have run together. Russia struck Ukraine's largest Danube grain port at Izmail, burning it and hitting its rail station, while drought across Europe dropped the Rhine and the Danube to levels that halted a reactor at Cernavoda. The FAO's food price index reached 131.1, and Sindh moved to import 5 million tons.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple grain for roughly half the planet and the one most tightly controlled by export policy. A few governments hold most of the exportable surplus, so a single export ban moves what billions pay to eat.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen against a broader food market moving the other way: the Food and Agriculture Organization's price index hit 131.1 in August as heatwaves and wars pushed up crop costs, while rice sits near the October 2025 low of $330.6 rather than the August 2024 peak of $563.8. The input does not explain the divergence.

copper.standing: The world benchmark price for refined copper, quoted per tonne. Copper is the metal grids, motors and buildings are wired with, so its price tracks electrification and construction demand and feeds through to the cost of everything that carries current.
copper.recent: Copper has run to a record 13,550 $/mt in June 2026, half again above its December 2024 low of 8,910. The demand side is visible in the grid build-out — Texas halted new data centre grid connections with 474 gigawatts of requests queued, five times peak demand — while supply stays slow to answer: the Mes Aynak deal signed in 2008 has produced nothing.

us-10y.standing: The yield on ten-year US government debt, the benchmark price of borrowing for the world's largest borrower. It sets the floor under mortgages, corporate credit and sovereign spreads everywhere, and moves on inflation, Fed policy and demand for Treasuries.
us-10y.recent: The yield sat near the top of its range after the BOJ held rates at 1% on 31 July while warning underlying inflation was running above its 2% target, the same day the series peaked at 4.75%. Since then the dollar fell to its weakest since May as a rate hike came into doubt, and Trump again moved to fire Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence.

sp500.standing: The main US equity benchmark, tracking 500 large listed companies weighted by market value, and the index most of the world's passive retirement money is invested against. Membership is decided by a committee, not a formula.
sp500.recent: Reddit rose 11% on the S&P Dow Jones Indices committee's decision alone, with inclusion set for August 18 — no earnings changed, but every fund tracking the index must buy before then. The series peaked at 7799 on Aug 13, up 5.17% over the window, with stocks gaining earlier in the month on Hormuz reopening hopes.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is the most concentrated public bet on large-cap technology, so chip, cloud and consumer-device earnings move it more than the broad market.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits near the top of its two-month range after a run of hardware and AI capital news: Nvidia arranged $500 billion in financing through six lenders for buyers of its chips, Amazon backed a Texas gas plant to power a datacentre, and Apple's China-only AI model was cleared by regulators in Beijing.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump, surveyed weekly across the country. It follows crude prices with a lag of a few weeks, plus refining margins and state taxes, and it is the most visible consumer price in the United States.
us-gas-retail.recent: Refining capacity, not crude, has been the story: Ukraine hit two Russian refineries on 6 August and struck Nizhnekamsk on 10 August, killing 13; a third drone attack set Libya's Zawiya refinery alight on 11 August; and Saudi Arabia put out a fire at Aramco's Jizan facility. US pump prices still eased over the window.

natgas-ttf.standing: The benchmark price for natural gas traded at the Dutch TTF hub, the reference for most of Europe's gas contracts. It moves on pipeline supply, LNG cargo competition and weather, and heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: The series sits at 15.09 $/MMBtu, up roughly a quarter over the window and well above the 9.46 low of Dec 2025, after peaking at 17.67 in Mar 2026. The input does not explain the move.

vix.standing: A gauge of how much volatility options traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from index option premiums. It falls when markets are calm and spikes when they are frightened, which is why it is read as a fear index.
vix.recent: The gauge has drifted steadily lower over the past three months, from 22.22 on Jun 10 to a low of 14.55 on Aug 12, a decline of roughly a fifth. The input does not identify what drove the calm, though the same quiet extends beyond equities: bitcoin volatility nearly vanished in early August even as ETFs took in $754 million.

fx-pkr.standing: The exchange rate of Pakistan's rupee against the US dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel, edible oil and machinery in dollars, so the rate sets the domestic price of imported energy and food and the cost of servicing external debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has been close to flat over the past month, trading in a narrow band between 278.2 on Jul 22 and 276.6 on Jul 31 to sit at 277.2. Nothing in the record explains a move of that size, because there was not one — the pressure showed up in prices rather than the rate, with diesel at 383.95 rupees a litre and gold at $4,392 an ounce.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the US dollar. Nigeria imports most of its refined fuel and much of its food, so the naira's level sets domestic prices, and oil export earnings in dollars are the main thing supporting it.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira firmed slightly over the month, easing from 1,381 on Jul 22 to 1,358. Abuja is forgoing tax to unlock $50 billion in deep offshore oil investment, and the Senate has issued an ultimatum to oil firms after Seplat Energy skipped its own audit hearing — both bearing on the export earnings that back the currency.

fx-egp.standing: The exchange rate of Egypt's currency against the US dollar. Egypt imports most of its wheat and fuel, so the rate sets the domestic price of bread and energy, and it governs the burden of the state's dollar-denominated debt.
fx-egp.recent: The pound has traded in a narrow band, easing about 1% over the month from 51.37 on Jul 25 to 49.56 on Aug 8 before settling near 50. Nothing in the month's Egypt news — the Cairo talks on the Gaza plan, the widening feud with Ethiopia over the Red Sea — carries a monetary decision that would explain the drift.

fx-try.standing: The Turkish lira against the US dollar. Turkey runs large external financing needs and imports most of its energy, so the rate transmits directly into domestic inflation, and the central bank's independence is the thing markets price when it moves.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to 47.9 per dollar, its weakest of the month, as Turkey took on exposure on several fronts at once: the Mecca defence pact signed with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, a Kurdish disarmament law, and rationed Bosphorus passage after a Turkish cargo ship was hit near a Russian port. The move was gradual, not a break.

fx-bdt.standing: Bangladesh's currency, quoted as taka per US dollar. It prices the country's garment export earnings and its imports of fuel, food and machinery, and it is managed rather than freely floated, so its moves tend to come in steps.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka has drifted back to 122.5 per dollar after touching 124 on 7 August, a move of about half a percent across the month and no sharp break in either direction. The month's political news out of Dhaka — the government pressing Delhi over its stance ahead of Hasina's planned speech, and India's denial of involvement — did not register in the rate.

fx-idr.standing: The exchange rate of Indonesia's rupiah against the dollar, the price of Southeast Asia's largest economy. A commodity exporter with foreign-currency debt, Indonesia feels dollar strength in its import bill first, and the central bank in Jakarta manages the currency accordingly.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah firmed through the month, reaching 17,790 on Aug 17 after a high of 18,110 on Jul 28. The clearest domestic marker was Prabowo's nomination of a Bank Indonesia deputy as the central bank's new governor on Aug 11, on which the currency rose slightly. The magnitude-7.7 Flores earthquake that killed 53 left no visible mark on the rate.

fx-lbp.standing: The Lebanese pound's exchange rate against the US dollar. Since the 2019 banking collapse it has traded far below its old peg, and because Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine, the rate sets the price of nearly everything sold there.
fx-lbp.recent: The rate has barely moved, drifting between 89,180 on Jul 31 and 89,720 on Aug 7 — a range of well under one percent — even as the truce with Israel frayed. Strikes continued through the seventh round of direct talks in Rome, and an attack near Ansar killed seven on Aug 15. The currency has absorbed none of it.

fx-cny.standing: The yuan's exchange rate against the dollar, managed by China's central bank within a daily trading band rather than left to float freely. It prices the output of the world's largest exporter, so it moves the cost of goods, commodities and debt far beyond China.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted stronger across the month, from 6.775 on Jul 19 to 6.742 on Aug 17, a move of under half a percent. Nothing in the month's China news explains it: the period was dominated by the death of former premier Zhu Rongji, tightened drone export controls, US accusations of tariff evasion, and China's coast guard patrols east of Taiwan.

fx-inr.standing: The rupee's price against the US dollar. India imports most of its crude oil and pays for it in dollars, so a weaker rupee raises the cost of fuel, fertiliser and electronics at home and lifts the earnings of its export-facing IT and refining firms.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee has firmed about 1% over the month, from 96.64 on 19 July to 95.05 by 5 August, a stretch that included crude falling 4.5% on one remark about Iran — cheaper oil eases India's largest import bill. It has since drifted back to 95.58, with July retail inflation at 4.45% from 4.38% in June.

fx-brl.standing: The exchange rate between Brazil's real and the US dollar, the price of the largest economy in South America. It sets the local cost of imported fuel and machinery, and moves with commodity prices, interest-rate gaps and political risk.

fx-mxn.standing: The exchange rate between the Mexican peso and the US dollar, and one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends most of its exports north, so the rate tracks the health of the US trade and remittance relationship.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened through a month of friction with Washington rather than despite it: the US put a $25 million bounty on a Jalisco cartel leader, and on 14 August cancelled the US visa of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, drawing a public rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum. None of it touched trade terms, and the currency reached 17 to the dollar on 17 August.

fx-eur.standing: The euro against the US dollar — the second-most traded currency pair in the world, and the price at which the eurozone's exports, energy imports and cross-border debt are settled. It moves on the gap between what the ECB and the Federal Reserve do with interest rates.

fx-jpy.standing: Japan's currency, quoted as yen per dollar, and one of the world's most traded. A weak yen inflates the earnings Japanese exporters bring home and raises the cost of the fuel and food the country imports.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen's strongest point in the window followed a joint US-Japan intervention confirmed on 3 August, which pushed the dollar to a one-month low and reversed the slide from 163.9 on 26 July. It has since drifted back toward 159.3. Toyota, reporting quarterly profit of $9.4 billion, was among the exporters banking the cheap-yen windfall.

fx-rub.standing: The exchange rate of Russia's currency against the dollar, set inside a capital-controlled financial system rather than a free market. It is the clearest single price on how much oil revenue the country earns and how much imports cost.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble weakened through mid-August as strikes multiplied on both sides: Ukrainian drones hit the Samara rocket plant and the Novorossiysk naval base and port, Russia says it downed 822 drones overnight, and a Wildberries depot near Moscow burned. Lavrov rejected freezing the war at the current front line.

fx-zar.standing: The currency of South Africa, priced against the dollar, and the most heavily traded currency in Africa. It carries the country's mining exports and its politics, and moves on both commodity demand and the state of domestic institutions.
fx-zar.recent: The rand strengthened from 16.83 on 25 July to 16.15 on 8 August, its floor for the month, before settling at 16.17. The domestic news in this window ran to policing and procurement — soldiers deployed in Cape Town where 70 people were killed in a week, and the Prasa security-contract investigation in Pretoria — rather than to anything that would move the currency itself.

btc.standing: The price of one bitcoin, the oldest and largest cryptocurrency, quoted in dollars around the clock. It has no issuer and no central bank, so it moves on flows, custody failures and regulation rather than earnings or policy rates.
btc.recent: The month's fall runs through a run of custody and platform failures rather than any macro turn: the Coldcard hack drained $120 million and congested the mempool with the attacker's own transactions, and a separate exploit emptied Foundation's and Citadel21's Lightning nodes. Bitcoin fell 4% on 3 August against every other market signal, and Russia's ban on Moscow mining until 2032 followed on 15 August.

eth.standing: The second-largest cryptocurrency by value, and the settlement layer most stablecoins, tokenised assets and decentralised exchanges are actually issued on. Its price moves with crypto risk appetite, and with the rules written for the market it hosts.
eth.recent: Ether has drifted inside a narrow band, with the low on Aug 2 set as prices declined into a fifth day of the Coldcard exploit and recovering as those sweeps receded. Since then the market has traded on rulemaking rather than incident: the SEC scrapped Friday's Reg Crypto vote, leaving jurisdiction unsettled, while Bernstein warned Clarity Act failure could spark another selloff.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by physical gold in vaulted bars, tracking the price of an ounce. Gold is the asset money moves into when currencies, inflation or policy look unreliable, so its price reads as a gauge of that distrust.
paxg.recent: Spot gold hit $4,392 an ounce Wednesday as markets braced for US inflation data, carrying the token to its 31-day peak on Aug 13. The same week KPMG completed Tether's long-promised audit, counting the stablecoin issuer's gold bars by hand — a reminder of how much crypto collateral now sits in bullion.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A count of how many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is a rough gauge of public curiosity about the technology rather than of the technology itself, and it climbs when AI stops being an industry story and becomes everyone's.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Readership rose through a fortnight in which AI kept arriving in ordinary institutions: Spotify said it would stop promoting AI-tagged artists, Anthropic extended watermarking to text Claude only edits, and a Hartford legal filing was found to contain invisible text telling AI models to side with the plaintiff. The Aug 13 peak coincided with Seoul's $880 billion bet on AI infrastructure.

wiki-russia.standing: Wikipedia's article on Russia — the world's largest country by land area, a nuclear-armed permanent member of the UN Security Council, and a top exporter of oil, gas, grain and fertiliser. Daily readership tracks how far its actions reach.
wiki-russia.recent: Readership rose through a fortnight in which the war reached deep into both countries: a Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk killed at least 13 on 10 August, and drone strikes on Novorossiysk hit the naval base and port on 12 August. Putin then threatened cargo ship seizures from a warship off Sakhalin, and Lavrov rejected freezing the war at the current front line.

wiki-pakistan.standing: The Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a nuclear-armed South Asian state of some 240 million people. Readership rises when the country's politics, its border with India, or its role in wider regional security enters the news.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Attention followed the Mecca defence pact: on 7 August Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence agreement, described as a 'Sunni NATO', which the following week turned into a standing bloc of defence chiefs, foreign ministers and military heads. The peak on 29 July preceded that signing.

wiki-china.standing: The Wikipedia article on China, and a rough gauge of how many people worldwide go looking for background on the country on any given day. Readership climbs when China is the actor in a story rather than a mention in one.
wiki-china.recent: The spike to 13 August tracked a week in which China acted on several fronts at once: its coast guard began routine patrols east of Taiwan, the side of the island Hualien and Suao serve as fallback ports, while Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy in the same waters and Jakarta signed on to Beijing's Taiwan line. Zhu Rongji, the premier who restructured the state sector and took China into the WTO, died on 12 August at 97.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: A 39-kilometre-wide sea lane between Iran and Oman through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes. Nothing else connects Gulf producers to open water, so a threat to it is a threat to the price of everything shipped and burned.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership followed the closure standoff. Iran has kept the strait shut behind six conditions and a reparations demand, with transits down by a third and 8 to 15 ships crossing daily; Trump claimed in Washington that "We own it." The Guard Corps then said it downed a US MQ-9 Reaper over Hormozgan, and two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: The Wikipedia page for Saudi Arabia, the Gulf's largest economy and the world's biggest crude exporter, whose readership rises when the kingdom's security, oil or diplomacy is in play.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: Readership climbed through a week of Saudi security news: on 7 August Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan signed a joint defence pact in Mecca, and the same day Houthi missiles hit Yemen's oil provinces around Marib and a strike on Najran wounded 11, including a 4-year-old. Attention has since eased.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The Wikipedia article on the sitting US president, and one of the most-read biographies on the site. Its daily readership rises and falls with whatever the presidency is doing, which makes it a rough gauge of how much of the world's attention Washington is holding.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Attention through this window tracked Trump's Iran confrontation and its domestic aftershocks: his claim that the US fully controls the Strait of Hormuz on 3 August, the disclosure that he left Ankara hidden inside a catering truck under an Iranian threat, and a run of legal setbacks — a court halting his privately funded ballroom, a second attempt to remove Cook from the Fed.

wiki-india.standing: Wikipedia's article on India, and the number of people who open it each day. A country page of this size is read as a reference by students, travellers and anyone following a story out of the subcontinent, so its readership tracks whatever brings India into view.
wiki-india.recent: The peak on Aug 6 came as Odisha ran its Har Ghar Tiranga campaign into the Independence Day week that followed, when an Army band opened the Red Fort ceremony with Vande Mataram and Modi used the platform to promise eight more chip plants and nuclear reactors. Readership has since settled back near where the window began.

wiki-israel.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Israel — a baseline of how many people worldwide go looking for background on the country. It rises when Israel is at the centre of a story big enough to send people past the headline.
wiki-israel.recent: The peak on Aug 11 came as more than 500 attacks hit the West Bank in a week and Venezuela restored consular ties with Israel after 17 years. Attention held through the following days: soldiers removed villagers besieged by settlers at Qusra, and an Israeli strike near Ansar in south Lebanon destroyed a house and killed seven.

wiki-ukraine.standing: A daily count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine — a rough gauge of how much of the world is paying attention to the country at any given moment, and one that rises and falls with the war rather than with any market.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Readership has held near its range through a month of deep strikes in both directions: a Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk killed 13 on 10 August, Russia set Ukraine's largest Danube grain port at Izmail ablaze on 13 August, and on 16 August Russia said it downed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and its largest oil producer. Attention to a country page tends to move with the events that pull outsiders toward it.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Attention has fallen roughly a fifth from its 27 July peak to 6,184 views on 13 August. Nothing in this window explains the July high; the Nigerian news since has been domestic — Osun's contested vote, where 34 incidents and 18 deaths preceded Saturday's ballot and Adeleke's re-election, and an aviation shutdown as unions barricaded Air Peace terminals in Lagos.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic collapsed as the blockade hardened: Iran passed a statute targeting Hormuz transit, two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting the strait, and US Hellfire missiles crippled a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman. The last week runs 46% below the 90-day baseline, against a high of 44 vessels on Jun 24.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic has fallen with the Houthi campaign along both shores. A projectile sank the Indian-flagged MSV Faize Noore Oliya on 4 August, missiles and drones hit the Red Sea port of Mokha, and six sailors died in a strike on a cargo ship. Maersk, rerouting around the closure, raised profit guidance to $6.5 billion.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic sits near its 90-day baseline despite continued danger at the southern approach: six sailors died in a Bab al-Mandeb strike on a cargo ship, and a projectile sank an Indian-flagged vessel in the Red Sea. Maersk, which routes around the region, lifted full-year profit guidance to $6.5 billion.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Traffic sits near the low end of its range, running 14.9% under the 90-day baseline, and the recent extremes are two adjacent days: 28 vessels on 10 July, 401 on 12 July. Typhoon Dolphin, which forced flight cancellations and evacuations in China on 9 August, is the kind of closure that produces that pattern.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transits are running at 29 vessels a day, down about 15% across the window and 4.3% against the 90-day baseline, with a peak of 83 on Jul 13 and a low of 22 on Jul 22. Nothing in the record explains the swing.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic sits well below its own 90-day baseline as the Black Sea shipping war widens. Turkey has rationed passage, turning back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk, and TASS says Russia has struck 130 ships since July. A drone killed a crewman on a Turkish-owned coal tanker, and Ukraine hit the Novorossiysk naval base on 12 August.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic is down 30% across the window, from a high of 163 vessels a day on Jun 13 to 112 now, though the past week sits level with the 90-day baseline. Seas have been calm, waves topping out at 0.6 m. Nothing in the record explains the drop.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic sits at 168 vessels a day, about 2% below its 90-day baseline and well off the 210 recorded on May 23 — an ordinary summer drift rather than a disruption. Seas have been calm, with waves peaking at 0.6m. The Channel's news this month has been human rather than commercial: a dinghy carrying 157 people caught fire off Boulogne-sur-Mer on August 4.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Traffic ran a wide band across the window — a low of 68 vessels on Jul 4 against a high of 123 on Jul 31 — and the last week sits 5.8% below the 90-day baseline, with rough seas and waves to 3m on the route. The input does not name a cause for the swing.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Owners have abandoned the route. TASS says Russia has struck 130 ships since July, and Ukraine hit the naval base and port at Novorossiysk on 12 August; both sides have also hit each other's export terminals, from Izmail on the Danube to Ust-Luga. Traffic is now zero, 98% below its 90-day baseline.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The drift down through the summer runs alongside Houthi fire reaching Saudi soil: 12 missiles hit Yemen's oil provinces, a strike wounded 11 civilians in Najran, and Aramco fought a fire at its Jizan refinery, which processes 400,000 barrels of crude daily. Riyadh answered with a joint defence pact signed at Mecca with Turkiye and Pakistan.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits below its 18 June high after a crowded fortnight for Ankara: Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed a joint defence pact in Mecca on 7 August, parliament passed a law on Kurdish disarmament on 10 August, and Moscow protested a US-Turkey arms transfer to Ukraine. Turkey also rationed Bosphorus passage, turning back some vessels bound for Novorossiysk.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index has given up ground since its Jun 18 high of 6270, and August brought the reasons: seven blasts in twenty minutes at Jebel Ali, Dubai's transshipment port; two ADNOC tankers struck transiting Hormuz; and a forecast loss of 137,000 Gulf tourism jobs.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index has drifted down from its Aug 5 high of 1748 as the Hormuz closure reached Malaysian refineries, cutting Gulf crude arrivals to a fraction of normal volumes and forcing import substitution. Domestic politics added to the drag: Anwar Ibrahim's coalition lost Negeri Sembilan to a Malay-nationalist wave, and the DAP scheduled a vote on staying in the unity government.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: Prabowo's nomination of a central bank deputy as the next governor steadied the currency, and the rupiah rose slightly on the news. Since then the market has absorbed domestic shocks rather than financial ones: a magnitude-7.7 quake in East Nusa Tenggara that killed 53 and cut Sikka's only coastal road, and a ferry fire near Bali. The index sits below where it stood in May.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index sits well above its May low, helped by an exporter earnings run in which Toyota's quarterly profit nearly doubled to $9.4 billion on a cheap yen. That prop was pulled partly away in August, when a joint US-Japan intervention pushed the dollar to a one-month low against the yen.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index sits roughly where it started the window, having fallen to 22,670 on Jun 26 before recovering to 25,520. Nothing in the period's China news explains the swing: the deaths, drills and export fights — Zhu Rongji's death, Beijing tightening drone exports, US accusations of tariff evasion — did not move the tape in step.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits below where it started the window, its low on Jul 17 and a partial recovery since. Washington has accused Beijing of evading tariffs, and China tightened drone exports in a fresh trade clash, while Apple's regulator-cleared China model and Alibaba's 27-billion-parameter open release marked a stronger domestic tech line. Zhu Rongji, architect of the restructuring that carried China into the WTO, died on Aug 12.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The index sits well below its June high after a memory-driven selloff: SK Hynix dropped 5% on a $38 billion fab commitment, and all 2027 memory capacity is already sold out, concentrating the market on one bet worth $880 billion. Security news ran alongside it — North Korea resumed missile testing ahead of US-South Korea drills.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 64-day range after a policy-heavy week in New Delhi: the windfall levy on petrol exports was cut from ₹3.5 to nil, refiners' cooking-gas quotas were reset across 21 companies, and Modi used Independence Day to promise eight more chip plants. Reliance also moved into jet engines with Rolls-Royce.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed roughly a seventh over the past three months, reaching 5,754 on Aug 11 before easing to 5,722. Nothing in the window explains the run: the Singapore-datelined stories cover a hardware-wallet breach that leaked 39,798 buyers' addresses and steady Bab el-Mandeb shipping traffic, neither of which is an index-moving event.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index sits well above its 30 July low, but the run-up has come alongside a steady accumulation of pressure around the island. China's coast guard now patrols east of Taiwan, the side where Hualien and Suao serve as fallback ports, and Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy in the same waters. Taipei also says AI agents extracted passwords over four days last month.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits at the top of its 45-day range, having climbed steadily from the May low, and the domestic news of the period left no mark on it: a school shooting in Nonthaburi that killed eight and wounded 15, and Bangkok's decision to host Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing, moved politics rather than prices.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after climbing off a late-May low, but slipped on the day. Manila's politics have run through the period: the Sara Duterte impeachment trial reached Day 14 with confidential-fund disbursements logged to unusual names and zero results, and a magnitude 6.3 earthquake struck the southern Philippines on 5 August.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the high it set on Aug 6, having climbed roughly a twentieth over the window, though it slipped on the latest session. The RBA held its cash rate steady on Aug 11 as the housing market softened, and China's steel stock has aged enough to recycle — a shift toward scrap that skips Australian iron ore, the index's largest export earner.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The index has drifted about 2.8% lower over the past nine weeks, from a 7 August high of 117,500 back toward 114,100, with the low of 108,300 set on 23 July. Nothing in the available material accounts for the move.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index sits at its 66-day low of 166,900, down 6.4% from a mid-May peak of 178,400, with the drift running through weeks of friction with Washington: the US revoked the visa of Brazil's ambassador on 4 August, tying its restoration to Brasília accepting its own pick of envoy.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has drifted down through a run of US friction with Mexico City: Washington cancelled Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa, drawing a public rebuke from Claudia Sheinbaum, and offered $25 million for a Mexican cartel leader. A screwworm outbreak passing 500 human cases adds a hit to the livestock trade.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index has climbed roughly 7% over the window, reaching its high of 36,760 on Aug 13, and has been effectively flat since. The input does not identify what drove the rise.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index sits near its high after a committee at S&P Dow Jones Indices added Reddit, whose shares rose 11% on the decision alone — roughly half of US equity money is passive, so every tracking fund must buy before 18 August regardless of what it thinks of the company. Little else in the period touched prices.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index reached its highest level of the period on Aug 14, up roughly 8% since May. Bank shares had support from Commerzbank saying a tie-up with UniCredit could create value, a deal Berlin had previously called a sovereignty threat. Little else in the window points at Frankfurt directly.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index climbed to 8,726 on Aug 10 and has held near that level since, gaining about 7% over the window with no single French event behind it. The period's domestic news ran to power and courts rather than earnings: jellyfish swarms knocked out 3.2 gigawatts of nuclear capacity at Gravelines on Aug 11, and three of France's 57 reactors shut in July as heat derated the grid.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index climbed through the period to a high of 1120 on Aug 13, up roughly nine percent over the window, before easing slightly. Shell agreed to sell its European onshore renewables business on Aug 3, the one corporate move in the window at that scale. Nothing else in the record explains the rise.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index reached 20,210 on 11 August, near the top of a run of roughly 13% since a 17,620 low on 15 May. Nothing in the Spanish news of the period explains the climb: the domestic stories were the Ceuta crossings, where 72,000 people entered a city of 84,000, and reciprocal border checks with Italy — neither of which touched the listed banks and utilities that dominate the index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index sits near the top of its 67-day range, having climbed roughly 7% from its 19 May low of 48,360 to a 7 August high of 53,720. Nothing in the record explains the run: the Italian news of the period was Spain's reciprocal border checks, the resignation of three directors at the space agency, and Milan-based Bending Spoons buying Airtable for $1.28bn.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range, up about 9% over the window and roughly a fifth of a percent below the 14,630 high set on Aug 10, after a low of 13,220 on Jun 3. The available material does not explain what drove the climb.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after climbing roughly 8 percent from its 15 May low of 3036, peaking at 3327 on 5 Aug before easing. The coverage in this window does not explain the move.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

wiki-spain.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Spain — a proxy for how many people worldwide are looking the country up, which rises when something there pulls a global audience toward the basics.
wiki-spain.recent: The August 12 total solar eclipse ran its path of totality across Spain, the first in Europe in 30 years, and readership peaked well before it as people looked up where to go — Burgos, Teruel and Zaragoza each sat under the path for under two minutes. By August 12 itself, the day of the eclipse, the series had fallen back to its low.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the US Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at a given meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with anything that shifts the odds of a cut or a hike — inflation prints, labour data, and pressure on the Fed itself.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The contract has climbed through August after Trump again moved to fire Fed governor Cook, reviving the fight over Fed independence, and traders looked past the CPI print to the Fed's next tests. It ran from 39 on Aug 1 to 75 on Aug 15.

wiki-turkey.standing: A count of how many people open the Wikipedia article on Turkey each day — a rough gauge of when a country stops being background and becomes something outsiders go looking up.
wiki-turkey.recent: Turkey signed a collective-defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan on 7 August, described in coverage as a possible 'Sunni NATO', with Egypt absent and each state's commitments left undefined. Ankara then passed a Kurdish disarmament law on 10 August, and Moscow objected to US missiles reaching Ukraine via Turkey.

poly-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-e.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether US-Iran negotiations get a 60-day extension. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves as the diplomatic track visibly opens or closes rather than on any official statement of intent.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Israel and Iran hold a ceasefire by a set date. It pays out on the fact, not on opinion — so the price is what traders are willing to stake that the shooting has actually stopped.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The price climbed from 26 on Jul 19 to a 96 high on Aug 17, tightening as the war moved from strikes to statutes: Iran now legislates Hormuz control through a statute rather than a blockade, and Kushner met Hamas leader Al-Hayya in Cairo to push the Gaza peace plan. The contested claims are rhetorical now — a $30,000 bounty, Ben-Gvir's kill quota — not new fronts.

xag.standing: A silver-backed digital token priced against a troy ounce of physical silver held in vault, so it tracks the silver price. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial input, which is why its price is more volatile than gold's.
xag.recent: The series moved from a low of 29.8 on Aug 6 to a high of 66.52 on Aug 15, and stands at 65.3. Nothing in the available material explains the move.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves on candidacy news, coalition shifts and polling — not on any official count.

poly-trump-out-as-president-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Donald Trump ceases to be US president before 2027 — by death, resignation, removal or incapacity. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it is one of the few continuously quoted measures of political tail risk in Washington.
poly-trump-out-as-president-before-2027.recent: The contract has drifted down over the past month, from 8% on 18 July to 6% on 16 August, with no discrete event behind the slide. What news there was ran the other way: an Iranian security-commission chairman, Ebrahim Azizi, told Trump to worry about his own security amid the Hormuz dispute, and a decoy plane swap in Ankara drew scrutiny CIA analysts gave low confidence to.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Vladimir Putin will cease to be Russia's president before the end of 2026. It prices political risk at the top of a nuclear-armed state — the one variable that reprices Russian assets, energy supply and the war all at once.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: The odds have drifted down through a month in which the war escalated without touching the Kremlin's position. Russia said it downed 822 Ukrainian drones overnight on 16 August, and strikes reached Moscow, the Samara rocket plant and the Novorossiysk naval base — while Lavrov rejected freezing the war at today's front line.

wiki-venezuela.standing: A count of how many people open the Venezuela article on Wikipedia each day — a rough gauge of how much of the world is paying attention to the country at once, and one that tends to move with political ruptures rather than with slow-burning conditions.
wiki-venezuela.recent: Attention has fallen by roughly a quarter since the July peak even as the consequential work continues: government and opposition wrapped up a first round of post-Maduro talks in Caracas on 13 August, closing on the courts and frozen money, while María Corina Machado hired a Republican lobbyist in Washington.
